_roadWidth: MEASURED off the painted lane, not assumed: the median clearance from the cyan centre stroke to the nearest pixel that is not road, doubled. Narrowest 22.2 and widest 46.2 canvas px on the half-width; the median is the honest number because the lane has to fit its narrowest stretch. Level 1's road is 80.0, so this one is 18% tighter and every lateral figure derived from it moves with it.
note: EVERY NUMBER HERE IS DERIVED FROM tools/level2_path_overlay.png, which is the volcanic plate with the lane's centre stroked in cyan and fifteen tower pads ringed and numbered in green. That is the difference from level 1: this plate came with its route drawn on it, so nothing here is a classifier's guess about what is road. Re-derive with `python3 tools/check_level2.py --emit` after any re-export, and check the stored file against the art with `python3 tools/check_level2.py`. The overlay lives under tools/ and NOT under public/, because everything in public/ is deployed whether or not anything references it and this is 1.9MB that only that one script opens. VERIFY THE OVERLAY BEFORE DERIVING FROM IT: the correct file has 9641 pixels matching R<60 G>200 B>200. A superseded export went round with its cyan stroke one pixel thinner (7623), and because roadWidth is a median of integer distances measured along that stroke, deriving from it silently moved roadWidth 65.8 -> 67.6 and the waypoint count 49 -> 47 while the painted route had not moved at all.
_waypoints: Douglas-Peucker at 1.1 overlay px over the traced centre of the cyan stroke. MEASURED, not asserted: check_level2.py walks the painted centreline and reports the worst distance from it to this polyline, and that number is 1.0 OVERLAY px (0.9 canvas px) against a stroke four px wide, so the route is inside the paint for its whole length. The note used to claim 0.6, which was a number from an earlier epsilon that nothing re-measured after the epsilon moved — a file documenting a figure its own check disagreed with. THE TWO END POINTS ARE EXTENSIONS, NOT TRACED: enemies walk in from off the plate at x=-60 and out at x=1340, and each of those is a new point on the line the lane is already travelling when it reaches the edge. Level 1 drags its end waypoints out to those x values in place, which is free on that plate because its lane meets both edges flat. This lane arrives on a slope, and the same drag swung the opening segment 13 overlay px off the paint.
_buildSpots: 10 HAND-PLACED PLOTS, from tools/plots.json, written here by tools/apply_plots.py. THEY ARE NOT THE SCORING PASS's ANY MORE: the sweep's 90-114 px standoff band and its best-first ordering produced the set this replaced, and a person placed these against the painting instead. Every figure below that is a function of the pads was re-derived from THIS set off the centrelines this file ships; the sweep's own parameters (`padRules`, `padStandoffBand`, `padSpacing`, any `candidatePositions`) are left as the record of a pass that no longer chooses anything. tools/check_plots.py re-checks the road clearance, the plate edges and the tap-target spacing.
